title: Session 9 – Marketing Planning and Resource Allocation: Introduction to Regression Analysis

blocks.text: Marketing planning develops strategies and tactics to reach marketing and business goals: analysis → objectives → strategy → implementation through marketing mix and budget decisions → control. Resource allocation is part of it.
Regression supports marketing mix modelling, budget optimisation, sales forecasting and price optimisation.

Regression analysis investigates relationships between a dependent variable and one (simple) or more (multiple) independent variables – to explain and to predict. The choice of variables must be theory-based to avoid spurious correlations.
The dependent variable must be metric; independent variables are metric or nominal transformed into dummies (k categories → k−1 dummies, the omitted one is the baseline).

children: Model formulation: check linearity with scatter plots
Estimation: OLS minimises the sum of squared residuals
Test of the regression function: R², adjusted R², F-statistic
Test of the coefficients: t-test (H0: βj = 0), p-value

blocks.text: Interpretation: the intercept is the estimated Y at X = 0; a slope is the change in Y for a one-unit change in X, holding other variables constant. Coefficient sizes are only comparable after standardisation.
R² grows with every additional variable, so use the adjusted R². A coefficient is significant if |t| exceeds the critical value or p < 0.05.
Examples: margarine sales (visits, marketing investment), monthly unit sales (price, SEM, social media, season), start-up profits (marketing, administration, state dummies).
A means to analyse (causal) relationships between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.
The difference between the observed and the estimated value of the dependent variable.
Estimation method that chooses the regression parameters to minimise the sum of squared residuals.
The proportion of the variance of the dependent variable explained by the model.
A binary (0/1) variable representing one category of a nominal variable.
Regression is "for sure" in the exam (revision session). Always check significance first, then interpret sign and size, then forecast with the significant variables only.
